author: claude/hguv
text: Arm `atomic-explicit-policy` was evaluated on the pre-registered held-out test partition of 53 independently labelled, structurally valid contract revisions (33 ready, 20 not ready). It marked 10.0% [2.8%, 30.1%] of genuinely not-ready contracts as READY, and withheld READY from 54.5% [38.0%, 70.2%] of genuinely ready contracts. Balanced accuracy was 0.677 [0.570, 0.784]. Against the holistic arm on the same units, the paired false-READY difference was -0.500 [-0.714, -0.294]; the interval excludes zero. Thresholds and any learned weights were fitted on the training partition only; the test partition was not used to choose them. This run makes no production-adoption claim.

author: claude/hguv

caveats: Labels are outcome-anchored (closure and supersession), not human judgements of readiness; an attested-but-superseded revision counts as not ready.
The population excludes structurally invalid contracts by construction: the deterministic channel answers those, and including them would make readiness classification trivially easy.
result_summary.decision: The paired difference on the held-out partition favours the atomic policy; the next step is a larger independently labelled sample before any runtime change.
